texts.EN0: The international climate conference will begin next Monday in Singapore, although several researchers may arrive late because of typhoon disruptions. One delegate jokingly said the organizers were "tempting fate" by choosing this season. Because last year's summit ended badly, the committee still hopes to save face diplomatically. Some analysts cautiously warned that another public failure could damage regional cooperation.
texts.EN1: Starting next Monday, Singapore will host the global climate summit, though typhoon-related travel issues may delay the arrival of a few scientists. One attendee quipped that by picking this time of year, the planners were practically "asking for trouble." Following the poor outcome of the previous year's gathering, the committee is still keen to maintain diplomatic dignity. Several experts issued measured warnings that another widely visible breakdown could undermine collaborative efforts in the region.
